items.stem: Why is the design-build-test-learn (DBTL) cycle emphasised in synthetic biology?

options.text: Biological systems are complex and unpredictable, so iterative cycles are needed to refine designs
options.rationale: Correct: DBTL handles biology's variability through repeated design, measurement and learning.

options.text: Because biological designs always work perfectly on the first attempt
options.rationale: They rarely do; iteration via DBTL is precisely why the cycle matters.

options.text: Because DBTL avoids any need for measurement
options.rationale: The 'test' stage is measurement; it is central, not avoided.

options.text: Because DBTL replaces biology with pure software
options.rationale: DBTL guides engineering of real biological systems, not their replacement.

items.explanation: Correct: DBTL handles biology's variability through repeated design, measurement and learning.

items.stem: Which TWO are responsible principles when working in or reviewing synthetic biology? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Applying appropriate biosafety and containment measures
options.rationale: Correct: containment and biosafety protect people and the environment.
Correct: biosecurity guards against deliberate misuse.

options.text: Publishing step-by-step protocols for creating dangerous agents
options.rationale: This is unsafe and irresponsible; it enables harm.

options.text: Skipping oversight when a project 'feels' low risk
options.rationale: Oversight should not be skipped on gut feeling; governance applies regardless.

items.explanation: Correct: containment and biosafety protect people and the environment.

items.stem: What does treating a gene as a standardised 'part' aim to achieve conceptually?

options.text: A reusable, characterised building block that can be combined into larger designs more predictably
options.rationale: Correct: standardisation and abstraction aim to make biological engineering more modular and reusable.

options.text: A guarantee that the part behaves identically in every organism
options.rationale: Context-dependence means parts do not always behave identically across hosts.

options.text: A way to remove all unpredictability from biology
options.rationale: Standardisation reduces but cannot remove biological unpredictability.

options.text: A legal patent that prevents any study of the gene
options.rationale: Standardisation is an engineering idea, not a prohibition on study.

items.explanation: Correct: standardisation and abstraction aim to make biological engineering more modular and reusable.
